subject: Cross-region burst recovery - scope variance request
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@greenleafpay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@greenleafpay.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: hard RTO/RPO for multi-region burst failover

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. To summarize Greenleaf's ask: because we run transaction-sensitive routing for merchant payouts, we need a contractual commitment for multi-region failover behavior during high-burst events. Specifically we're asking Redwood to commit to the following for our production workload (primary region us-west2, standby us-east1):

- RTO (time-to-recover to serving traffic after regional outage): 15 minutes
- RPO (maximum data loss acceptable): 1 minute
- End-to-end tail latency SLA (p95) for single-region serving at steady state: <= 180ms

We understand this is outside the standard hosted SLA. Please advise feasibility, any architecture constraints you see, and an estimate of required reserved capacity or configuration we should purchase. We can share recent traffic patterns if helpful (I'll attach a short summary).

Also copying Aisha (our CISO) for the security/compliance angle — she may have follow-up on audit logging during failover.

Appreciate a quick read on whether Redwood can make these exceptions and what the cost/engineering tradeoffs are.

Best,
Morgan
Head of Platform Ops
Greenleaf Payments

Attachment: greenleaf-soc2-summary.pdf (summary, 1 page)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@greenleafpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@greenleafpay.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: hard RTO/RPO for multi-region burst failover

Morgan — thanks for the clear ask and the summary doc.

Short answer: we can work toward a contractual carve-out, but 15m/1m is very aggressive for an active/active failover across regions for a general hosted plan. There are multiple levers we can use to get close: dedicated capacity (pinned Dedicated clusters in both regions), synchronous KV replication for critical state, automated traffic cutover runbooks, and a small on-call escalation SLA.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll run this with Engineering (Karthik) to validate the operational path and quantize the RPO risk.
- Legal/Product (Laura) will draft a narrow addendum that ties the exception to committed reserved capacity and an agreed surge window.
- I'll share a proposed addendum and an estimated monthly delta for reserved GPUs and cross-region replication bandwidth.

Can you confirm the expected QPS and median token lengths for your latency-sensitive calls? If you can send a 24h sample we can size the Dedicated pool.

I'll aim to get a proposal over by Monday.

—Vanessa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: hard RTO/RPO for multi-region burst failover — engineering + legal review

Team — forwarding Greenleaf's ask. TL;DR: 15m RTO / 1m RPO; p95 latency target 180ms. They're on a payments flow; a failure impacts settlement windows.

Karthik — can we enumerate the options and a recommended target we can commit to if Greenleaf purchases:
a) Dedicated bi-regional reserved pool (active/active) + synchronous KV (cross-region) — expected achievable: RTO ~10-20m for full traffic cutover, RPO ~1-3m depending on state sync approach; cost: high due to always-on reserved capacity and network egress.
b) Active/passive warm standby (hot cache in standby, async replication) — expected achievable: RTO ~25-45m, RPO ~5-10m; lower cost but longer recovery and possible duplicate/dropped in-flight tokens.
c) Hybrid: Dedicated for control-plane + burst routing with pre-warmed instances and prefix/KV caching — expected achievable: RTO ~15-30m, RPO ~2-5m; medium cost.

Notes on latency: meeting p95 180ms requires placement (us-west2 edge) and smaller quantized model variants for heavy QPS. We should tie the p95 commitment to a pinned model+instance class in the addendum.

Laura — legal: we'll need an addendum that limits the carve-out to documented outage types (regional AZ outage / cloud region-wide) and includes an exception clause when we have cross-region network partitioning. Also propose limiting credits to a capped amount and requiring Greenleaf to maintain a minimal reserved throughput for the carve-out to apply.

I'm attaching a draft addendum skeleton and a quick cost sketch. Please review and suggest redlines.

Thanks,
—Vanessa

Attachment: proposed-sla-addendum.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@greenleafpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@greenleafpay.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: hard RTO/RPO for multi-region burst failover — proposed carve-out

Morgan / Aisha —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a proposed narrow carve-out that Redwood can offer for Greenleaf if you agree to the following binding commitments:

- Reserved bi-regional Dedicated capacity: minimum of 4x p4d-equivalent slots in us-west2 and 4x p4d-equivalent slots in us-east1 active in standby mode;
- Commitment term: 12 months;
- Synchronous replication for critical routing state (RPO bound to replication window): target 2 minutes under normal operating conditions;
- Agreed traffic shaping during failover (we will throttle burst QPS above a pre-agreed threshold to protect state sync);
- Tail latency (p95) guarantee limited to requests served from pinned region/model/instance class; exceptions apply during cross-region network partitions.

What we can commit to in writing in the addendum:
- Recovery target: RTO 20 minutes (measured from incident declared to routing cutover), RPO 2 minutes (measured by committed sync window) — subject to the Reserved Capacity terms above.
- Latency: p95 <= 180ms when serving from pinned region and model.
- Credit regime: limited to 6 months of monthly reserved delta, capped at the value of 3 months of reserved capacity.

If Greenleaf needs tighter RTO/RPO (15m/1m), the engineering delta is primarily more aggressive synchronous replication (and possibly stronger consistency guarantees from the application layer). That will require additional reserved capacity and protocol-level changes on their side to acknowledge writes only after durable cross-region confirmation. We can explore, but it becomes materially more expensive and operationally brittle.

Please review the attached addendum and let me know if you want us to:
1) proceed to legal redlines and generate a DocuSign envelope
2) run a DR tabletop in a staged window to validate the 20m/2m targets once agreed

If you confirm (1) I will route the DocuSign and include the HubSpot record and SOW references.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
